title: Best CAD Software in India 2026 (with Prices)
excerpt: A buyer's guide to the Autodesk CAD products TechZoid sells, from AutoCAD LT to Revit, Civil 3D and Fusion, with how to match each to your work.
body:
There is no single best CAD software for every Indian business. The right choice depends on what you make: 2D drawings, buildings, roads and sites, mechanical parts or products. This guide is honest about its scope: it covers the Autodesk CAD products that TechZoid Technologies sells as a reseller, with annual prices, and tells you which job each one fits. It is not a review of every CAD product on the market.

## What "best" means when buying CAD

Teams choose badly when they search for a winner. A fabrication shop and an architecture studio need different tools, and a software that suits one can be wasted on the other. Start with five questions:

1. What is the deliverable: a 2D drawing, a 3D model, a coordinated building model, or a manufacturing toolpath?
2. Which discipline: architecture, civil, mechanical, electrical, product design?
3. Who do you exchange files with, and in what format?
4. How many people need it, and how often does each open it?
5. What hardware do you have, and is it Windows or Mac?

Answer those and the shortlist usually shrinks to one or two products. Our [CAD software category page](/cad-software) lists everything we sell in this area, and [BIM software](/bim-software) covers building-model tools.

## For 2D drafting: AutoCAD LT and AutoCAD

If your output is drawings, start here. **AutoCAD LT** is cost-effective 2D CAD for drafting, drawing and documentation, and suits interior designers, contractors and small consultancies. **AutoCAD** is the full product: the drafting baseline across architecture, engineering and manufacturing, with 3D modelling and rendering, DWG comparison, sheet sets, and the seven industry toolsets (Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical, MEP, Map 3D, Plant 3D and Raster Design) included. It also carries the web and mobile apps.

The decision is covered in detail in [AutoCAD vs AutoCAD LT](/blog/autocad-vs-autocad-lt). In short: pure 2D, choose LT; 3D, toolsets or automation, choose AutoCAD. For pricing context, read [AutoCAD subscription price in India](/blog/autocad-subscription-price-in-india).

## For site and field staff: AutoCAD Web

[AutoCAD Web](/products/autocad-web) lets people draft, annotate and add field data to drawings in a browser or on a mobile device, working with DWG files. It suits site engineers, supervisors and reviewers who need to mark up a current drawing but do not need a full desktop seat. In a named-user world, where every person who opens the software needs a seat, this is a lower-cost way to cover occasional users.

## For buildings: Revit

[Revit](/products/revit) is a building information model rather than a drawing set. Architectural, structural and MEP elements exist as objects with real properties, and plans, sections and schedules are views of one model. It is the choice when a client requires BIM, or when coordination across disciplines matters. It runs on Windows only and needs real hardware: 16 GB of RAM at minimum and 32 GB or more for large models. It also takes adoption effort in templates and families. See [Revit vs AutoCAD](/blog/revit-vs-autocad) for the full comparison, and ask us about Revit LT, a simplified 3D BIM tool that is priced on enquiry.

## For roads, drainage and sites: Civil 3D

[Autodesk Civil 3D](/products/autodesk-civil-3d) handles model-based design of roads, drainage, earthworks and site grading, with surfaces, alignments, profiles and corridors that update their documentation when the design changes. It also imports survey data and produces plan and profile sheets. Civil and infrastructure consultancies in India often pair it with AutoCAD; it is included in the AEC Collection, so teams that also use Revit should price the collection before buying it standalone.

## For mechanical and product design: Inventor and Fusion

[Autodesk Inventor](/products/autodesk-inventor) provides product design and engineering tools for 3D mechanical design, simulation, visualisation and documentation. It suits engineering firms designing assemblies, machinery and components.

[Autodesk Fusion](/products/fusion-360) combines mechanical design, manufacturing toolpaths, simulation and electronics in one cloud-connected application. For product design and small-batch manufacturing teams, the integration is the point: a design change flows to the CAM toolpath without re-importing geometry. It runs on both Windows and macOS and needs a persistent internet connection for cloud data. Be aware that certain advanced manufacturing, simulation and generative design capabilities are licensed as separate extensions, so tell us your workflow before we quote. Our [Fusion page](/fusion-360) has more.

## Collections: when one person uses several products

A collection bundles several products for one named user. The [AEC Collection](/products/aec-collection) includes Revit, AutoCAD with its toolsets, Civil 3D, Navisworks Manage, Infraworks, 3ds Max, structural analysis tools and Autodesk Docs. The [Product Design & Manufacturing Collection](/products/autodesk-product-design-manufacturing-collection) is the equivalent for manufacturing teams. The commercial rule is simple: with one product per user, standalone is cheaper; with two it is roughly break-even; with three or more it usually wins. Read [the AEC Collection explained](/blog/autodesk-aec-collection-explained).

## Occasional users: Flex

If someone needs a product only a few days a year, a full subscription is expensive. Autodesk Flex lets you prepay tokens and draw them down as people use products. It is priced on enquiry, and the arithmetic is covered in [Flex versus named-user subscriptions](/blog/autodesk-flex-versus-named-user-subscriptions).

## Which CAD should you pick? Examples

- **Interior design studio, six people, 2D layouts:** AutoCAD LT.
- **Architecture practice delivering BIM to government clients:** Revit, or the AEC Collection if AutoCAD and coordination tools are also needed.
- **Highway consultancy:** Civil 3D, with AutoCAD for detailing.
- **Machine builder designing assemblies:** Inventor.
- **Start-up making consumer hardware with a small team:** Fusion, after checking whether you need extensions.
- **Site engineers who mark up drawings:** AutoCAD Web.

## How to match products to people, not to the company

The most expensive habit in CAD buying is picking one product for the whole company. A better approach is to list people by role and assign the lightest product that does their job well:

- **Daily 2D drafters:** AutoCAD LT or AutoCAD, depending on whether they need 3D or toolsets.
- **Model builders:** Revit, Civil 3D, Inventor or Fusion, depending on the discipline.
- **People who switch between products:** a collection.
- **Reviewers, site staff and managers:** AutoCAD Web, or Flex for occasional desktop use.

Autodesk's admin reports show how often each person opens each product. Look at that data before a renewal; the usual outcome is a few seats moved to cheaper options and a few moved up, rather than a simple cut.

## Hardware and file-format checks before you buy

CAD is hungry. AutoCAD asks for 16 GB of RAM at minimum, with 32 GB recommended for large drawings and 3D work, and a DirectX 12 capable GPU. Revit and Civil 3D need real workstations, and both are Windows only. Fusion is lighter, with a stated minimum of 8 GB of RAM and 16 GB recommended, but needs a persistent internet connection for cloud data. If you are specifying new machines, our workstation range is worth a look, and you should check Autodesk's current published requirements first.

On file formats, confirm what your clients and subcontractors exchange. DWG remains the common currency for drawings, while building teams may also ask for IFC exports from a BIM model. Agreeing this up front avoids awkward conversions late in a project.

## What this guide does not cover

Many CAD products exist beyond Autodesk, including free and open-source tools, other drafting packages, and specialist systems for large aerospace and automotive programmes. We have not reviewed them here and we do not rank them. If your clients, partners or sector already standardise on something outside this range, that is a legitimate reason to follow them. File compatibility matters as much as features, so ask what your counterparties use before you buy anything.

## Licensing, GST and buying in India

All the products above are licensed per named user: one subscription, one person, reassignable when someone leaves. Multi-year terms are generally cheaper per year than annual renewal, and monthly or multi-year terms can be quoted on request. Understand the model in [Autodesk named-user licensing: what changed](/blog/autodesk-named-user-licensing-what-changed). Every order carries a GST invoice at 18%, generally claimable as input credit for registered businesses.

Before you buy, check your workstation: specifications vary by product, so confirm current requirements on Autodesk's published pages. To see everything in one place, view our [price list](/price-list), then [ask for a quotation](/enquiry) with the number of users per role.

faqs.question: What is the best CAD software for a small business in India?
faqs.answer: It depends on the work. For 2D drawings, AutoCAD LT is the economical starting point. For 3D, toolsets and automation choose AutoCAD. Building design points to Revit, roads and sites to Civil 3D, and mechanical products to Inventor or Fusion.

faqs.question: Does this guide cover all CAD software on the market?
faqs.answer: No. It covers the Autodesk CAD products that TechZoid sells as a reseller, with annual prices. We do not review or rank other publishers' products. If your clients standardise on other software, compatibility with them is a valid reason to choose differently.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AutoCAD Web and AutoCAD LT?
faqs.answer: AutoCAD Web works in a browser or on a mobile device for drafting, annotating and adding field data to DWG files. AutoCAD LT is a desktop 2D drafting product. Web suits site staff and reviewers; LT suits people who draft every day. Compare them against each person's tasks.

faqs.question: Do Autodesk subscriptions include GST?
faqs.answer: Website prices exclude GST. GST is 18% on software and is added on the invoice, which is generally claimable as input credit for GST-registered businesses. A written quotation fixes the final price, since website prices are tentative.

faqs.question: Should I buy a collection instead of individual products?
faqs.answer: Only if each person genuinely uses two or more products in it. With one product per user, standalone costs less. Around two products it is close to break-even, and with three or more the collection usually wins. We compare against your usage before quoting.

faqs.question: Can I rent CAD software only for a few months in India?
faqs.answer: The catalogue prices here are annual. Monthly or other terms can be quoted on request, and for occasional users Autodesk Flex, priced on enquiry, may suit better than a full subscription. Send an enquiry describing how often each person works in the software.
